why: PROPOSED, task 575 / E575-1. NOT ratified: ratification is Tim's merge of
the POLICY PR, and until then this artifact is registered `proposed` and
only an experiment arm may select it.
v2 is unchanged in every predicate that decides WIDTH. The one change is
what P3 means. P3 exists to keep `chunk.law` out of the re-chunk campaign
(ADR-090 4, in both directions). It was written as a CALLER-ASSERTED
boolean -- `has_native_anchor` -- on the reasoning that the caller has the
record and the selector has only the markdown. Three callers then spelled
that boolean three different ways:
pipeline/chunk_reference_plan.py    bool(rec.anchor or rec.anchor_component)
(two experiment scripts)             bool(page.has_anchor or payload.anchor)
and `page.has_anchor` is `build_pages_565.py`'s
`bool(rec.anchor or rec.identity_anchor_component)`.
`identity_anchor_component` is the TIER-RESOLVED component from
`aw_b1_identity.classify_tier`: the native anchor for Tier A, the CONTENT
DIGEST for Tier B, "" for Tier C. For a Tier-B row it is never empty. So on
the staged rows that carry that field, P3's predicate evaluates
`bool(content_digest)` -- true of every row that has text.
WHAT THAT COST, MEASURED (task 575):
* task 572's own materialize.MANIFEST.json: P3 refused 206,707 pages, and
the per-store roll-up puts 206,707 of them -- 100.0%, across all 31
ADR-093 L1-b waves, no exception -- in the url-keyed L1-b lane, while
refusing 0 of the 19,762 sha256-keyed pages. A 100%/0% split across 46
independently built waves is structural, not a property of anchors.
* NOT ONE of the refused pages is a law family. Their source_types are
official (126,597), reference (41,240), docs (38,295), gov-tax, gov,
health, edu, entity-self; none is in the chunk.law deny list, and no law
wave is in the population at all.
* Four independent stages agree the lane carries NO source-native anchor:
the L1-b markdown records carry `anchor: null`; the corpus store's own
`anchor` column is empty on 100% of the rows of all 25 domains the 33
named golds sit on (53,990,262 rows cross-tabbed, conserved 1:1);
the staged rows carry `anchor` non-empty ZERO times in 1.8M rows over 62
shards; and `aw_e8` payloads carry no `anchor` key at all (390/390).
* The lane refused is at `rule_epochs.chunk: 4` -- the epoch-4 generic
width whose 3.73x granularity drop is the entire reason `chunk.reference`
exists. P3 was refusing the population the policy was written for.
So the predicate did not detect a source-native anchor; it detected which
staging era wrote which field name (`identity_anchor_component` vs
`anchor_component`). This artifact fixes the CLASS rather than the lane: the
question moves from the caller's spelling to the record's own anchor field,
read through the one home for the predicate.
THIS IS STILL NOT A HOST LIST AND STILL NOT CIRCULAR. P3' reads one field on
the record. It does not read the gold set, the incumbent collection, a
retrieval rank, a host name or a row count, and
`test_the_selector_reads_no_outcome_signal` still asserts that against the
module's own source.

generic_policy.note: Unchanged from v2. The incumbent rule; every width predicate is stated relative to what THIS policy does to the page.

reference_policy.note: Unchanged from v1 and v2. This amendment changes WHICH PAGES are eligible, not how wide the policy cuts, so the A/B still has one variable.

P3_no_source_native_anchor.rule: the record carries no SOURCE-NATIVE anchor and its source_type is not in the chunk.law deny list
P3_no_source_native_anchor.supersedes_in_v2: P3_no_native_anchor -- 'the record carries no source-native anchor', decided from a caller-asserted boolean
what_counts_as_a_source_native_anchor: The fragment THE SOURCE gave the passage: a fedlex Akoma Ntoso eId
(`art_336`), a legifrance article id, a cantonal `#art-2-3-5`. Read from
the record's own `anchor`/`native_anchor` field, with exactly the guards
`classify_tier` applies before it returns Tier A: non-empty, not the
literal string 'None', not positional (`chunk-5` shifts on any insertion
above it), and not equal to the record's own title (a page label is never
a chunk anchor -- the A33 trap).
A TIER-RESOLVED IDENTITY COMPONENT IS NOT ONE.
`classify_tier`, which is the content DIGEST for Tier B and "" for Tier
C. They are not read at all under this rule. That single sentence is the
derivation: ADR-090 4's scope bound is unchanged and is the reason P3 exists:
'standardize on 1152' is scoped to chunk.generic and 'may never be read as
authority to sweep chunk.law into the generic policy'; the same bound binds
this policy in the other direction. What the bound names is a family whose
boundaries ARE its own article anchors. A page with no anchor anywhere in
its record has no such boundary to protect, so refusing it protects
nothing and costs the whole density class it was written for.
The deny list on `source_type` is UNCHANGED and still decides on its own,
so a law family remains out of scope by name even where a record's anchor
field is empty for some other reason.
No threshold is introduced. This predicate has no number in it.
P3_no_source_native_anchor.one_home: pipeline/aw_b1_identity.has_source_native_anchor -- the same module that owns classify_tier, so the selector and the identity minter cannot disagree about what a native anchor is. The selector does not re-implement it (engineering-doctrine 1/6).
P3_no_source_native_anchor.refuses_rather_than_defaults: Under this rule `classify()` without a `record=` raises. A default of False would silently ADMIT every law article whose caller forgot to pass the record -- the failure this predicate exists to prevent, arrived at from the other side (verification-doctrine 6).

derivation: ADR-090 amendment 1's mechanism, carried over verbatim. At a gain of 0 the
two policies produce the same boundaries, the same text and the same
content-bound point ids, so there is nothing to supersede. Not re-derived
here: this artifact changes P3 and only P3.

excluded_by_construction.chunk.law_by_source_type: The deny list (ch_cantonal_law, ch_zh_fulltext, fedlex, law, statute) is unchanged and refuses on its own, before any anchor is read.
excluded_by_construction.chunk.law_by_anchor: A record that DOES carry a source-native anchor is refused exactly as v1 and v2 refused it. Measured corpus-wide, that is 383,375 of 53,990,262 rows (0.71%): fedlex 61,176 at 100.00% anchored, ch_cantonal 311,326 at 99.98%, de_laender 10,928 at 100.00%, plus 19,409 non-law rows that genuinely carry one -- huggingface.co 6,039, pytorch.org 5,675, scikit-learn.org 3,150, insee.fr 2,737, docs.jax.dev 1,672. Those stay refused, and that is the point: P3' is narrower than 'admit everything', it is 'admit what has no anchor'.
excluded_by_construction.chunk.news: Unchanged from v2: the exclusion is by FAMILY at the roster, not by a row's `source_type`.
excluded_by_construction.chunk.atomic: The source record IS the passage boundary. There is no markdown page to re-cut.
excluded_by_construction.chunk.preserved: The text was recovered, not produced (task 505).
excluded_by_construction.pages with zero sections: parse_sections returns [] and chunk_markdown returns []; there is nothing to classify.

reporting.every_page_gets_one_verdict: chunk.reference | chunk.generic, with the failing predicate named. ADR-086's shape applied to a classifier.
reporting.p3_evidence_is_carried: Every verdict's reasons name the `native_anchor_rule` in force and the anchor value it read, so a run under this artifact and a run under v2 are distinguishable from the verdict alone rather than from the config path.
reporting.tokenizer_note: Unchanged from v2. `generic_chunks` is tokenizer-sensitive; a run without the real tokenizer classifies a different corpus and must refuse rather than report (verification-doctrine 6).
